title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Ava Patel
summary: Centralized, company-wide policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs) covering access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policy, and internal templates. This page is the canonical reference and index for teams and people-ops to follow for compliant, auditable operations.
content:
Overview:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for core cross-functional functions: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended for all employees, managers, and approvers.

Sections:
1) Access & Permissions
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access, consistent onboarding/offboarding, and auditable access grants across cloud, internal tools, and private deployments.
Owners: Security & Compliance (policy), People Ops (process), Engineering managers (approvals).

Access tiers (table):
- Tier: Admin | Typical roles: Platform Admins, SRE Leads | Controls: 2FA mandatory, audit logging, quarterly attestation
- Tier: Prod-Operator | Typical roles: Service Owners, On-call Engineers | Controls: Scoped IAM roles, just-in-time (JIT) elevation, access expiry by default 30 days
- Tier: Read-only | Typical roles: Analysts, Support | Controls: Read-only tokens, limited to monitoring & billing data

Key procedures (numbered):
1. Onboarding access: Manager opens People Ops onboarding form -> selects required tiers -> Security issues initial credentials -> owner requests specific role grants via access request workflow (Jira/ServiceNow) -> Access expires default 30 days unless escalated.
2. Offboarding: HR triggers offboarding -> People Ops disables SSO account within 4 hours -> Security revokes cloud keys and service tokens within 24 hours -> Service owners confirm removal from team groups.
3. Temporary elevation (JIT): Engineers request elevation via access request ticket, approval required from service owner + security reviewer, max duration 8 hours for emergency fixes.
4. Quarterly attestation: Role owners receive attestation emails; stale or unneeded grants are removed.

Required artifacts and proofs for audits:
- Access request tickets (linked)
- Approved attestation logs
- Cloud IAM snapshot (monthly export to secure bucket)

2) Change Management
Purpose: Reduce risk from configuration and code changes to production systems while enabling rapid delivery.
Owners: Eng-Platform (process), Eng-SRE (operational gating), Security (risk review).

Change categories:
- Emergency: Fix impacting availability/security. Approval: SRE on-call + Eng-Platform manager. Post-implementation review required within 48 hours.
- Standard: Routine infra/infra-as-code and non-customer-facing configuration changes. Approval: Automated CI gating + peer review.
- Major: Architecture or infra changes with risk > medium (examples: model-serving topology changes, database migrations). Approval: Change review board (CRB), risk assessment, scheduled maintenance window.

Process (numbered):
1. Submit change RFC (template provided below) with rollback plan, SLO impact analysis, owner, and schedule.
2. Automated checks: CI, security scanning, preflight smoke tests.
3. Approvals: required approvers listed on RFC based on category.
4. Deployment: follow runbook and use feature flags / canary when applicable.
5. Post-change: validate SLOs and create a short postmortem for any anomalies.

Service-level thresholds to watch during change windows:
- API P95 latency: baseline +20% allowed during maintenance window
- Error rate: <1% for non-degraded services; any spike triggers rollback procedures

3) Data Management
Purpose: Protect customer and company data, ensure compliance with retention and residency commitments, and provide clear data lifecycle ownership.
Owners: Security & Compliance (policy), Eng-Infra (controls), Product (data classification decisions).

Classification categories: PII, Confidential, Internal, Public.

Retention & residency rules (table-like list):
- PII: retention only as required; encrypted at rest and in transit, KMS keys managed per-customer when requested; retention policy: default 90 days unless contract specifies otherwise.
- Confidential: model metadata, internal evals, audit logs. Retention: 2 years, access restricted.
- Internal: internal docs and runbooks. Retention: 5 years.
- Public: marketing, blogs. No retention constraints.

Data handling requirements:
- Encryption: All customer data in cloud and private deployments must be encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
- Access controls: RBAC + least privilege; use service tokens with rotation policy (90 days) and short-lived credentials for compute workloads.
- Backups: Monthly snapshot (cold) and daily incremental where applicable; backup manifests stored in encrypted artifact store.

Data incident response: follow Security incident response playbook (link in related_pages). Notify Product and Legal within SLA: 4 hours for confirmed data compromise.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Purpose: Standardize purchasing, approvals, and expense reimbursements to maintain financial controls and vendor visibility.
Owners: Finance & Legal (policy), Procurement (process), People Ops (travel expenses).

Procurement thresholds and approvals:
- <$2,000: Team lead approval via procurement portal.
- $2,000- $25,000: Department head + Finance approval.
- >$25,000: Executive sponsorship + Finance + Legal review; contract required.

Process (numbered):
1. Request submitter opens procurement request (ProcureFlow) with justification, budget code, and vendor info.
2. Procurement validates vendor onboarding & insurance certificates.
3. Finance issues PO or card provisioning.
4. Goods/services receipt and three-way match for invoicing.

Expense policy (summary):
- Travel: reimbursable per Travel policy below; receipts required for all expenses > $25. Corporate card preferred for hotel/airfare.
- Meals: capped at $80 per person (domestic) unless pre-approved.
- Software subscriptions: require procurement tag and approval before purchase to ensure license management.

5) Vendor Management
Purpose: Maintain vendor risk profile, SLAs, and compliance with contractual commitments.
Owners: Finance & Legal (contracts), Security (security review), Procurement (vendor operations).

Vendor lifecycle steps:
1. Preliminary vendor evaluation: business justification, budget, alternative analysis.
2. Security questionnaire: completed for vendors with access to sensitive data or infrastructure.
3. Contract negotiation: Finance & Legal lead; include SLA, data residency, incident notification clauses, and liability caps.
4. Onboarding: add to vendor registry, set owners, and configure monitoring (billing, usage alerts).
5. Quarterly vendor review: performance, spend, security posture.

Vendor risk scoring (example factors): data access scope, uptime SLA, historical incidents, financial stability. High-risk vendors require annual re-certification.

6) Travel Policy
Purpose: Safe, cost-effective, and compliant travel for business needs.
Owners: People Ops (policy), Finance (expense processing).

Key points:
- Booking: Use company travel portal (Concur) for all business travel; corporate rates encouraged.
- Pre-approval: Trips > $1,000 or requiring international travel need manager pre-approval.
- Safety: Employees traveling internationally must register trips with People Ops and provide emergency contacts.
- Insurance: Company-sponsored travel insurance covers medical evacuation for approved trips.

Reimbursement rules (short):
1. Submit receipts within 30 days via expense portal.
2. Meal per diem: $60 domestic, $100 international (defaults; manager exceptions possible).
3. Exceptions: luxury upgrades require prior approval and are not reimbursable unless pre-authorized.

7) Internal Templates and Forms
This section collects canonical templates to ensure consistent submissions:
- Access Request template (required fields: requester, owner, resource, duration, justification).
- Change RFC template (required fields: summary, impact, rollback, test plan, SLO impact).
- Procurement request template (fields: vendor, cost, budget code, procurement owner).
- Incident postmortem template (fields: timeline, impact, root cause, remediation, owners).

Embedded template examples (short):
- Change RFC (one-line): "Summary: [what] | Owner: [team] | Window: [time] | Rollback: [steps] | SLO impact: [p50/p95/error]"
- Access Request: "Requester: [name], Resource: [service], Tier: [Admin/Prod-Operator/Read-only], Duration: [days], Approver: [owner]"

Governance and review cadence:
- This document reviewed quarterly by People Ops and Security; material changes require Legal review.
- Annual tabletop exercise covering a change management emergency + data incident will be scheduled by Eng-SRE.

Related references and links:
- Security incident response playbook: /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security
- Vendor registry: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process (restricted)
- Change RFC template: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records

Contact and escalation matrix:
- Policy owner (People Ops): Ava Patel (people-ops@redwood-inference.internal)
- Security contact: Michael Chen (security@redwood-inference.internal)
- Procurement: procurement@redwood-inference.internal

Appendix: Quick checklists
- Onboarding checklist: Account created, SSO enabled, required groups granted, cloud keys rotated, initial training completed.
- Pre-deployment checklist for Major change: RFC approved, smoke tests green, backup taken, rollback verified, paging runbook assigned.
